name: Computer Networks
description: Layering, the data link layer, IP addressing and routing, TCP and UDP, application protocols and network security.

nodes.name: Layering
nodes.desc: The OSI and TCP/IP models, what each layer does and the units each layer exchanges.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe the OSI and TCP/IP models, what each layer does and the data unit each layer exchanges.

nodes.name: Switching & delays
nodes.desc: Circuit and packet switching; transmission, propagation and queuing delay in store-and-forward networks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare circuit and packet switching and compute transmission, propagation and queuing delays end to end.

nodes.name: Framing & bit rates
nodes.desc: Asynchronous transmission with start and stop bits, framing and bit stuffing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute effective bit rates for asynchronous transmission and apply framing and bit stuffing.

nodes.name: Error detection
nodes.desc: Parity, checksums, CRC by polynomial division and Hamming codes for correction.
nodes.summary: You will be able to detect errors with parity, checksums and CRC and correct single-bit errors with Hamming codes.

nodes.name: Stop-and-wait
nodes.desc: Stop-and-wait ARQ and link utilisation in terms of transmission and propagation delay.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse stop-and-wait ARQ and compute link utilisation from transmission and propagation delays.

nodes.name: Sliding window
nodes.desc: Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat, window sizes and the sequence-number bits they need.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat and calculate window sizes and the sequence number bits they need.
topics: Sequence number bits for each protocol

nodes.name: MAC protocols
nodes.desc: ALOHA, CSMA/CD and Ethernet minimum frame size, and token passing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse ALOHA, CSMA/CD and token passing and compute Ethernet's minimum frame size.

nodes.name: Bridges & switches
nodes.desc: Learning bridges, switches and the spanning tree protocol.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how learning bridges and switches forward frames and how spanning tree prevents loops.

nodes.name: IP addressing
nodes.desc: IPv4 addresses, classes, subnetting, CIDR and longest-prefix-match forwarding.
nodes.summary: You will be able to subnet IPv4 networks, use CIDR notation and forward packets with longest prefix matching.

nodes.name: IP fragmentation
nodes.desc: Fragmenting datagrams to fit the MTU: offsets, flags and fragment sizes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fragment IP datagrams to fit an MTU and compute fragment offsets, flags and sizes.
topics: More fragments and don't fragment flags

nodes.name: IPv4 header
nodes.desc: IPv4 header fields, TTL and the header checksum.
nodes.summary: You will be able to interpret IPv4 header fields, including TTL and the header checksum.

nodes.name: ARP, ICMP, DHCP, NAT
nodes.desc: The supporting protocols: ARP, ICMP and traceroute, DHCP and NAT.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how ARP, ICMP, traceroute, DHCP and NAT support IP networking.

nodes.name: Routing
nodes.desc: Routing tables and how routers compute them; intra- and inter-domain routing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how routers build routing tables and distinguish intra-domain from inter-domain routing.

nodes.name: Distance vector
nodes.desc: Distance-vector routing, Bellman-Ford updates and the count-to-infinity problem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run distance-vector routing updates with Bellman-Ford and explain the count-to-infinity problem.

nodes.name: Link state
nodes.desc: Link-state routing with flooding and Dijkstra, as in OSPF.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe link-state routing with flooding and Dijkstra's algorithm as used in OSPF.

nodes.name: UDP & sockets
nodes.desc: Ports, UDP's connectionless service, and the socket API.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain ports, UDP's connectionless service and how applications use the socket API.

nodes.name: TCP
nodes.desc: TCP's reliable byte stream, segments, acknowledgements and flow control.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how TCP provides a reliable byte stream with segments, acknowledgements and flow control.

nodes.name: TCP connections
nodes.desc: The three-way handshake, sequence numbers, wraparound and connection teardown.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace TCP connection setup and teardown and reason about sequence numbers and wraparound.

nodes.name: Congestion control
nodes.desc: Slow start, congestion avoidance, timeouts and the congestion window; token-bucket shaping.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace TCP's congestion window through slow start, congestion avoidance and timeouts and apply token-bucket shaping.

nodes.name: Application layer
nodes.desc: Client–server and peer-to-peer applications and which transport they use.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare client-server and peer-to-peer applications and match common applications to TCP or UDP.

nodes.name: DNS
nodes.desc: Name resolution, iterative and recursive queries, and DNS caching.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain DNS name resolution with iterative and recursive queries and how caching speeds it up.

nodes.name: HTTP, FTP & email
nodes.desc: HTTP persistent and non-persistent connections, FTP, SMTP and POP3.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare persistent and non-persistent HTTP and explain how FTP, SMTP and POP3 work.

nodes.name: Network security
nodes.desc: Threats, firewalls, symmetric encryption and hash functions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe network threats and defences such as firewalls, symmetric encryption and hash functions.

nodes.name: Public-key crypto
nodes.desc: RSA, Diffie–Hellman key exchange and digital signatures.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute RSA operations, perform Diffie-Hellman key exchange and explain digital signatures.
